Capability map · Diagram Design

Payments platform · which domain owns what

Four tiers, five named domains, forty-one capabilities, zero arrows. The domain box is the unit you point at in a meeting: membership says what it is composed from, and the two rails say what constrains and supports all of it at once.

THE HEADLINE

One router under six payment methods

Every method inside the payment-center domain reaches the provider channels through a single router. That is why it is drawn as a bar spanning its domain rather than a seventh chip beside them — and why one team owns every method-level incident.

Reading the map

  • Tier order is call direction, never importance
  • A named box is a domain with an owner
  • A bar spanning a domain means there is exactly one
  • Faded chips at the bottom are other people's rails

Why two rails

Risk control constrains every tier; shared services supply every tier. Neither can be stacked without claiming a call order that does not exist, and the flank they sit on is what tells the two concerns apart.
